audiolog_sky_laws_of_form.text: You know what I mean by a tree, in the mathematical sense?

audiolog_sky_laws_of_form.name: acting
audiolog_sky_laws_of_form.text: You can keep growing the branches of this tree,

audiolog_sky_laws_of_form.name: acting
audiolog_sky_laws_of_form.text: replacing one thing with another via incremental rewrites,

audiolog_sky_laws_of_form.name: acting
audiolog_sky_laws_of_form.text: expanding the expression for as long as your patience permits.

audiolog_sky_laws_of_form.name: acting
audiolog_sky_laws_of_form.text: And the Dao is very patient.

audiolog_sky_laws_of_form.name: acting
audiolog_sky_laws_of_form.text: With all our doodling, we've just created

audiolog_sky_laws_of_form.name: acting
audiolog_sky_laws_of_form.text: a huge proliferation of elaborate forms. All from just crossings and restatements.

audiolog_sky_laws_of_form.name: acting
audiolog_sky_laws_of_form.text: These forms we wrote, when reduced again, all boil down to Distinction or No Distinction --

audiolog_sky_laws_of_form.name: acting
audiolog_sky_laws_of_form.text: but the tree structure you can create has a huge number of possibilities.

audiolog_sky_laws_of_form.name: acting
audiolog_sky_laws_of_form.text: A countably infinite jungle.

audiolog_sky_laws_of_form.name: acting
audiolog_sky_laws_of_form.text: This gives you some insight into a small part of what we study here.

audiolog_sky_laws_of_form.name: acting
audiolog_sky_laws_of_form.text: Think on this, and we'll speak again soon.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2.text: As we've discussed, our Universe produces a tremendous proliferation of material.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2.text: We study these productions and we show what we find to others.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2.text: It may seem that, to take this activity seriously, we must show everything. But the contrary is true,

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2.text: because much of the material we discover can seem dry, repetitive, obscure. Hard to appreciate.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2.text: We people, we are short-sighted and weak.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2.text: Even artificially strengthened people, like myself. (And you, of course, if you play your cards properly.)

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2.text: People have limited attention spans. So, *after* we perform our design excursions and find these dispassionate nuggets of interestingness,

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2.text: it is a significant portion of our Art, which is not to be underestimated,

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2.text: that we work out how to frame the ideas to make them entertaining to our Visitors.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2.text: Because if everyone is just bored, or confused, they don't *see*.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2.text: So we sift for material that is interesting, satisfying, delightful.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.text: A primary indicator of interest is surprise:

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.text: as a Player, you didn't know where a puzzle was going; it seemed mysterious, or impossible;

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.text: but then BAM, with an insight, you see the answer, and it's something really interesting and new.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.text: There's a moment of clarity. In that moment, you become someone greater,

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.text: + instant_duration 5.5 because your mind is now enlarged; it now holds something special that it didn't before.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.text: So, how do we create moments of surprise?

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.text: Can you surprise someone with a puzzle full of objects chosen completely at random?

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.text: After all, nobody could expect that exact combination of things!

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.text: But there's nothing delightful about a box of junk; compositions that are *too* random feel like a mess.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.text: Also, random things feel the same as each other, so a sequence of them offers nothing new as it goes along.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.text: On the other hand, if the arrangement we make is too spare, too flat,

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.text: you can see everything about it on the first look. Clearly, there will be no surprise there either.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.text: Our composition needs to be on the edge of the Visitor's understanding,

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.text: so that the trick of the arrangement, its surprise, is beyond him at first, but then, with effort, he can pull himself across the gap.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.text: Real enjoyment comes when the surprise is not arbitrary, like which direction to go in a maze,

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.text: but rather, if it reveals something salient about the world you're in that you didn't already know.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_2_surprise.text: This particular fact is scarcely taken seriously outside our Order.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: Surprise seems to be special.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: If the world were completely predictable, there would be nothing to figure out or decide, as everything would be known to you.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: But, such a world would be too simple to be interesting. Certainly it could contain no humans.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: If the world were *too* random and chaotic -- we wouldn't have any idea what could happen next.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: How do you get food, shelter, safety, when you have no idea what *is* food,

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: and if you do figure that out, the world changes so quickly that your discovery becomes invalid in the next moment?

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: Fortunately, we're somewhere in the middle. The world operates according to rules, and those rules generate patterned outcomes.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: Those patterns are recognizable and predictable. So we humans have developed an extensive set of skills,

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: that are all about having expectations. Predicting what we think will happen next.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: And when our expectations are defied, the result is *surprise*.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: Sometimes surprise can be very delightful; sometimes it is horrifying and we die.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: That we often *do* find surprise enjoyable, some would believe is a mere biological

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: function. But many of us regard it instead as a deep mystery.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: sokoban
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: Its being biological makes perfect sense. To be surprised is to discover

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: sokoban
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: something wrong or incomplete in one's understanding of the world;

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: sokoban
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: it's beneficial to repair those mistakes.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: sokoban
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: Positive emotion helps anchor the moment of surprise in memory --

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: sokoban
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: that we may revisit it frequently, dwell upon it, and improve our understanding. If we do *not* do so, future surprises could kill us.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: sokoban
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: Thus creatures with positive feelings about surprise die less, and reproduce more.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: I think that's true, insofar as it goes. But consider there may be more to it.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: We've said that Reality is always combining the elements we *already have* and producing things *never before seen*.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: Perhaps the *point* of this involves surprise at seeing new results.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: Perhaps the Universe is engaged in a constant process of generating its own delight, and we mere humans,

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: when we solve some puzzle and feel a moment of joy in understanding,

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: perhaps we are just tapping into that background delight, harmonizing with it,

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: experiencing a brief insight into the fundamental nature of reality.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: acting
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: Perhaps strengthening that connection is a skill we can learn.

audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.name: sokoban
audiolog_sky_play_of_form_3.text: Well. I am here to listen.

end2_sokoban_writing_choice_1.name: sokoban
end2_sokoban_writing_choice_1.text: You should know that I've been watching your progress throughout the Overworld.

end2_sokoban_writing_choice_1.name: sokoban
end2_sokoban_writing_choice_1.text: I apologize for what may seem an invasion of privacy. It's the way they do things here.

end2_sokoban_writing_choice_1.name: sokoban
end2_sokoban_writing_choice_1.text: For me, it's been tremendously instructive, watching you grapple with these same problems that I myself faced not long ago.

end2_sokoban_writing_choice_1.name: sokoban
end2_sokoban_writing_choice_1.text: I am somewhat new here. I have a direct overseer watching me, as I am watching you.

end2_sokoban_writing_choice_1.name: sokoban
end2_sokoban_writing_choice_1.text: You heard her earlier, during the first Endgame. She does not want me to communicate with you directly.

end2_sokoban_writing_choice_1.name: sokoban
end2_sokoban_writing_choice_1.text: Non-communication is a strict rule usually, which she broke for my sake, but we're enforcing it again. We are not supposed to pollute you, you see.

end2_sokoban_writing_choice_1.name: sokoban
end2_sokoban_writing_choice_1.text: I enjoy dictating my thoughts, as may be obvious by now;

end2_sokoban_writing_choice_1.name: sokoban
end2_sokoban_writing_choice_1.text: but when you enter this next Endgame, I'll be using written Signs to indicate the course of action.

end2_sokoban_writing_choice_1.name: sokoban
end2_sokoban_writing_choice_1.text: Eventually we may discuss why. For now you'll have to take it as given.

end2_sokoban_writing_choice_2.name: sokoban
end2_sokoban_writing_choice_2.text: As I have previously mentioned, I had a choice whether to dictate or to write Signs, and I chose to write.

end2_sokoban_writing_choice_2.name: sokoban
end2_sokoban_writing_choice_2.text: There was then, naturally, a further choice: how *much* to write.

end2_sokoban_writing_choice_2.name: sokoban
end2_sokoban_writing_choice_2.text: If I wrote at great length, I could be very specific in pointing out every detail that I wish you to observe.

end2_sokoban_writing_choice_2.name: sokoban
end2_sokoban_writing_choice_2.text: But I prefer to use the nonverbal channels, when I am able to employ them successfully.

end2_sokoban_writing_choice_2.name: sokoban
end2_sokoban_writing_choice_2.text: So I chose brevity, to give space for the Puzzles themselves to speak.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_1.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_1.text: This representation of me, they call a 'hologram', though where I come from, the corresponding word indicates a mirage made only of light.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_1.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_1.text: But as you can feel, this 'hologram' is solid. Once I've reached a certain rank I'll be taught the sciences that make it possible.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_1.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_1.text: In this area, inert Signs are no longer sufficient for the level of communication we wish to provide.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_1.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_1.text: The hologram will draw upon a wider variety of pre-written responses.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_1.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_1.text: It is also a somewhat more-personal substitute for my presence.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.text: As with the previous Endgame, she gave me a choice of medium:

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.text: She said I could communicate via writing, or imbue the hologram with voice.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.text: Voice would make the hologram more lifelike, as though I were speaking to you directly;

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.text: and it would add nuance to the communications, via inflection, pacing and all that.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.text: But I felt voice to be the wrong mode here.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.text: In these Puzzles, when you are not quite sure of the answer,

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.text: you may try many different possibilities and see what I have to say of each.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.text: If my hologram's responses were vocal, I think it would become tiring to receive the same response five times in a row;

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.text: And, you must stand there listening awhile, merely to discover whether the response has changed!

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.text: You hear the first few words, and wonder: "is this the same response I heard last time,

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.text: or one that begins with the same words, but changes towards the end?"

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.text: You listen for some duration, just to realize there is no new information.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.text: Thus your attention is spent to no purpose, and you have a little less energy to exert on the Puzzles.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.text: I do not like that, and I don't think you would either; the repetition would become grating.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.text: When the response is visual, as when written on a Sign,

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.text: it can be inspected in an instant; and, it's no surprise when a Sign *doesn't* change.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.text: I think she approved of my reasoning, though it would be outside the rules

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_2.text: for her to discuss it until this process is complete.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_3.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_3.text: You are seeing this place as a battery of challenges prepared for you,

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_3.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_3.text: and it is; but it's also a test for me.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_3.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_3.text: How well did I communicate via my hologram's responses?

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_3.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_3.text: Did I anticipate all that you may try? Did I miss any situation that should have been met with a customized response?

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_3.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_3.text: Am I good enough to guide you through, or will I step on your toes mid-dance?

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_4.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_4.text: In the course of authoring the hologram's responses, I needed to learn the system of reasoning they developed for these purposes --

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_4.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_4.text: it's quite a thing, creating a mechanism that can sense the positions of objects,

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_4.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_4.text: shunt this information through some complex permutations of ... connectedness, and in the end decide which feedback to give.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_4.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_4.text: Where I came from, we had perhaps the beginnings of this kind of reasoning;

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_4.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_4.text: but here, they've laid out entire fields of research around each seemingly simple idea,

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_4.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_4.text: the existence of which a layman would never foresee.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_4.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_4.text: These techniques amount to setting down a sequence of instructions to be performed by an automatic device.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_4.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_4.text: It sounds simple enough. And it is, while the sequence remains short.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_4.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_4.text: But as the sequence becomes longer, the system begins to exhibit behaviors

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_4.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_4.text: you did not foresee, and certainly do not wish to occur.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_4.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_4.text: No. It's really not simple at all. But I am learning rapidly.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_5.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_5.text: Seeing as you've made it here, this means that, beginner though I am,

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_5.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_5.text: the quality of my work has proved sufficient.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_5.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_5.text: This is a success for me. I shall move forward. Thank you for that.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_5.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_5.text: Perhaps someday I will be given the chance to design my own Warehouse, and you may try it;

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_5.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_5.text: but before that can happen, there's a problem they must solve that lies beyond my present learning.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_5.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_5.text: The Director -- the still-titular Director -- said that erosion comes slowly at first,

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_5.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_5.text: barely noticeable; then it accelerates, and before you can blink, it's a landslide.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_5.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_5.text: But if decay can come quickly, perhaps it can go quickly.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_5.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_5.text: I'll endeavor to advance, that soon I may actually help.

end3_sokoban_writing_choice_5.name: sokoban
end3_sokoban_writing_choice_5.text: Thank you for walking with me. As my mentor is fond of saying: See you later, Alligator.

all_together_now_reassembly_1.name: sailor
all_together_now_reassembly_1.text: There's been a change. He wants to reassemble us.

all_together_now_reassembly_2.name: sailor
all_together_now_reassembly_2.text: He'll meet with us soon. We're supposed to save someone's life!

all_together_now_reassembly_2.name: sailor
all_together_now_reassembly_2.text: He's put together a plan, and we're going to ... rehearse?

end3_skipping_1.name: boat
end3_skipping_1.text: I'm here to see you through this final phase.

end3_skipping_1.name: sailor
end3_skipping_1.text: But ... how do *you* know what's happening?

end3_boats.name: boat
end3_boats.text: Did you ever imagine we'd see a place such as this?

end3_queen_promesst_red.name: queen
end3_queen_promesst_red.text: I cannot account for it... but I have the strange sense that I've been here before.

promesst1_gems_amount1.name: gemsman
promesst1_gems_amount1.text: As I'd hoped. They shut down in such a panic, they just left all the gems.

promesst1_gems_amount2.name: gemsman
promesst1_gems_amount2.text: Why'd they shut the mines down? What were they afraid of?

promesst1_gems_amount3.name: gemsman
promesst1_gems_amount3.text: It's not greed. These will be very valuable ... in research.

promesst1_gems_amount4.name: gemsman
promesst1_gems_amount4.text: Well, I *will* sell some of these. But it's not greed.

promesst1_gems_amount5.name: gemsman
promesst1_gems_amount5.text: I *will* sell some of these, but it's to hire a staff, help with the research.

promesst1_gems_amount5.name: gemsman
promesst1_gems_amount5.text: The proceeds will not be spent frivolously.

promesst1_gems_amount6.name: gemsman
promesst1_gems_amount6.text: The proceeds will not be spent frivolously.

promesst1_gems_amount6.name: gemsman
promesst1_gems_amount6.text: Though ... I deserve some comfort too. For all my grit and toil.

promesst1_gems_amount6.name: gemsman
promesst1_gems_amount6.text: It's hard to summon great ideas when the rent falls due and the wallet is empty.

promesst1_gems_amount7.name: gemsman
promesst1_gems_amount7.text: It seems there's no stopping me!

promesst1_further_down.name: gemsman
promesst1_further_down.text: There *should* be a way further down. Maybe that big round stone was placed to seal it?

promesst1_further_down.name: gemsman
promesst1_further_down.text: And that high-mounted beamcaster unseals it somehow?

queen_og_heroes_entry.name: queen
queen_og_heroes_entry.text: Though ... I had thought thus about my own walls.

queen_og_wardrobe_2.name: queen
queen_og_wardrobe_2.text: The cloth feels smooth and well-tailored. And I feel like ... a new person.

queen_og_first_green_beam.name: queen
queen_og_first_green_beam.text: Not sure I'll ever get used to this, not when it's happening to *me*.

queen_og_first_lily.name: queen
queen_og_first_lily.text: Well, that was a cute ride.

queen_og_gold_room_first.name: queen
queen_og_gold_room_first.text: Seems like a place they want me to notice.

audiolog_u_old_games.name: director
audiolog_u_old_games.text: Like most cultures, we started with primitive games -- objects like cards, or little wooden men,

audiolog_u_old_games.name: director
audiolog_u_old_games.text: and rules about what the cards mean, where the men can go and what happens as a result.

audiolog_u_old_games.name: director
audiolog_u_old_games.text: As our technology advanced, so did our games.

audiolog_u_old_games.name: director
audiolog_u_old_games.text: I know that you have gears that can shift into and out of conjunction.

audiolog_u_old_games.name: sokoban
audiolog_u_old_games.text: Yes. The doorstead we developed uses hundreds together.

audiolog_u_old_games.name: sokoban
audiolog_u_old_games.text: Fitting them all, and keeping them precisely tuned, presented a serious challenge!

audiolog_u_old_games.name: director
audiolog_u_old_games.text: Imagine you had very special gears, spinning at billions of revolutions per second.

audiolog_u_old_games.name: sokoban
audiolog_u_old_games.text: Thousands of millions? It's unimaginable. The size, the immense heat, and the *noise*! Would they not ignite the very air?

audiolog_u_old_games.name: director
audiolog_u_old_games.text: These gears are very small, you could neither hear nor see them.

audiolog_u_old_games.name: director
audiolog_u_old_games.text: You put together a billion such, shifting into and out of relation,

audiolog_u_old_games.name: director
audiolog_u_old_games.text: and you can develop quite a system of rules for your game.

audiolog_u_old_games.name: director
audiolog_u_old_games.text: The players no longer have to enforce the rules themselves --

audiolog_u_old_games.name: director
audiolog_u_old_games.text: the gears perform the logic, representing the objects and their interactions,

audiolog_u_old_games.name: director
audiolog_u_old_games.text: and now you can make games whose rules are far too complex and interdependent to administer by hand.

audiolog_u_old_games.name: director
audiolog_u_old_games.text: When this kind of system was invented, the space of games that could be created suddenly became vastly larger, compared to those days of cards and wooden men.

audiolog_u_old_games.name: director
audiolog_u_old_games.text: The people of that time made special screens that allowed them to see into those little game worlds --

audiolog_u_old_games.name: director
audiolog_u_old_games.text: "video" screens -- and thus the medium of "video games" was born, and flourished for a while.

audiolog_u_games_inspirations.name: director
audiolog_u_games_inspirations.text: As our technology advanced, so did our games. We always brought games with us,

audiolog_u_games_inspirations.name: director
audiolog_u_games_inspirations.text: through the upheavals and calamities that we were lucky to survive -- *seemed* lucky to survive.

audiolog_u_games_inspirations.name: director
audiolog_u_games_inspirations.text: What we do today, in these Warehouses, you couldn't call the same thing.

audiolog_u_games_inspirations.name: director
audiolog_u_games_inspirations.text: But it has its roots in the games of our elders,

audiolog_u_games_inspirations.name: director
audiolog_u_games_inspirations.text: and our Order holds this time in great respect.

audiolog_u_games_inspirations.name: director
audiolog_u_games_inspirations.text: Occasionally we look back and re-experience the works of that time, as best we can,

audiolog_u_games_inspirations.name: director
audiolog_u_games_inspirations.text: to return to a childlike state, to try and notice what we've lost in the modern day.

audiolog_u_games_inspirations.name: director
audiolog_u_games_inspirations.text: And sometimes, we do find litle nuggets of gold.

audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.name: director
audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.text: Though I hope for you to be a good keeper of this warehouse,

audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.name: director
audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.text: I always want people thinking of the next level up, also.

audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.name: director
audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.text: So here's something to consider as you observe, review, and maintain.

audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.name: director
audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.text: When we merge different worlds, they don't connect to each other automatically.

audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.name: director
audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.text: We must add cement between, to help them join; choosing the composition of that cement is our opportunity to exert authorial voice.

audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.name: director
audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.text: For example: You have the Wizard. In his own world, he is well-defined: He teleports around in such-and-such a way.

audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.name: director
audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.text: You have the magic Mirror. In its own world, it is well-defined.

audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.name: director
audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.text: Now the worlds come together. How is the Wizard to interact with the Mirror?

audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.name: director
audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.text: You have several choices.

audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.name: director
audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.text: You could say, the Mirror behaves as any old Stone, so the Wizard just swaps with it.

audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.name: director
audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.text: Simple. Clean. But boring, and irresponsible:

audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.name: director
audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.text: there's an eddy of potential there that's been ignored:

audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.name: director
audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.text: the Mirror has a shape. It's reflective in two directions.

audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.name: director
audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.text: What *should* this mean, with respect to the Wizard and the way he moves?

audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.name: director
audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.text: As an Implementor, you would get to decide.

audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.name: director
audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.text: Your decision may create new, additional vortices of behavior

audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.name: director
audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.text: that are delightful for a Visitor to explore.

audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.name: director
audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.text: Or, if your decision is not so good, the players may just find it dull, boring, contrived.

audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.name: director
audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.text: As you review your holdings, I'd like you to observe:

audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.name: director
audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.text: what are these choices that were made filling the gaps between the worlds,

audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.name: director
audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.text: and what do you, personally, think of those choices?

audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.name: director
audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.text: Would you have done it differently?

audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.name: director
audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.text: But really think it through, because it's easy just to say yes there, "Of course, *my* version would be better!"

audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.name: director
audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.text: Sometimes you'd be right.

audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.name: director
audiolog_u_wizard_mirror_worlds_connect.text: But you must always really think it through.

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.text: The Tetratetrad was originally Lemur's idea, but he prefers to keep his spindly hands off of day-to-day matters.

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.text: So, I must admit a decent amount of culpability.

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.text: I'll tell you the project was ridiculous beyond even what you've heard,

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.text: because the worlds inside each tetrad were chosen for maximum density —

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.text: with an unusual number of affordances, higher even than any of the worlds in this Warehouse.

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.text: More affordances per world means, when the worlds are connected, there are tremendously more arcs in the graph.

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.text: This tangle of arcs becomes very difficult to wrangle,

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.text: but it's the whole reason we're here, So we had to just eat the problem.

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.text: Once we had chosen some candidate worlds, we kept Tetrising the tetrads

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.text: to achieve maximum volume of the resulting product space. This was an iterative process.

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.text: Once things were drafted out, and we had a full system that we could operate and test,

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.text: we would often see opportunities to do better if we substituted some new world for an existing one.

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.text: Similarly for entire tetrads. We had a farm league of candidate tetrads that we had roughed out to various levels of completion,

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.text: and several of these drafts were swapped in and out of the four tetrad slots.

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.text: We continued to find new ways to pump up the density --

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.text: this meant we had engaged in a fair bit of wasted work,

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.text: as Implementors might work with a particular world for years, only to find it swapped out one day. Poof.

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.text: It's very easy to feel mistreated, and become frustrated.

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.text: But we all know why we're here: it's all to the glory of God.

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.text: So most of us got over our issues, and if you were open to it, it wasn't so hard to see the bright side:

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.text: "Hey, if your pet world didn't make it in, then after the four-four is done,

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.text: you can use that world in a different combiner. Your work won't be completely wasted. It's fine.

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.text: The real product here is the refinement of your soul,

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.text: not the object we construct, which is temporary, like all Earthly things."

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_1.text: We encouraged Implementors to accept this kind of reasoning, to help them remain sane, to avoid everything blowing up.

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.text: ... you see, it just wasn't good enough to curate a single beautiful world;

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.text: we were solving a global optimization problem containing many parts that interacted across multiple levels of abstraction.

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.text: To improve the mix, one could:

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.text: (a) Revise the selection of dynamics we borrow from a particular world: which people, which objects?

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.text: (b) Revise the rules that define the dynamics between foreign objects from different worlds

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.text: (lacking these rules, no possibility would be defined, so the objects could not interact at all)

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.text: (c) Substitute an entire world inside a tetrad, to achieve maximum cross-connectivity between the four worlds;

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.text: (d) Substitute an entire tetrad within the Tetratetrad;

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.text: ... And all the while, adapting all of the ten thousand individual puzzles

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.text: a Visitor would face -- because when you change the macro-scale shape of the whole thing,

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.text: this adds pressure in some places, relieves it in others, and the optimal form of any individual puzzle changes in response.

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.text: Because here's the thing: we're powerful, but we aren't magic.

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.text: We don't know how well a world, or an entire tetrad, is going to function, until we put it together and observe the outcome;

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.text: then we can work hard to iterate and push it further, again and again,

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.text: seeing how good we can make it in the limit, so we can then ask: Is this new idea truly better than what we had before?

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.text: Or should I scrap all this work I just did?

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.text: For us, the process of answering these questions can take years.

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.text: Puzzles were constantly being created, refined, discarded. Even the best of them.

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.text: Very beautiful puzzles were regularly dropped into Cold Storage, which was heartbreaking,

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.text: but it had to happen because the environment for which they were designed no longer existed,

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_2.text: and under the new arrangement they felt clumsy, incomplete, unsatisfying.

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_3.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_3.text: The Tetratetrad was certainly not the best place for a Visitor's first exposure to our work -- too dense, too hard to follow --

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_3.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_3.text: but if they'd done a good ten or twenty other Warehouses first, they could work their way up to it.

audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_3.name: director
audiolog_u_tetratetrad_troubles_3.text: For us, it was the brightest star in our crown. Or it would be, when finished.

audiolog_u_decay_1.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_1.text: The decay is eating into our Warehouses as though they were Swiss cheese.

audiolog_u_decay_1.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_1.text: And by studying that cheese, we hope to learn

audiolog_u_decay_1.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_1.text: how to protect the facilities we've built across these dozen decades, all seventy thousand of them,

audiolog_u_decay_1.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_1.text: so that the whole thing doesn't just shrivel and die.

audiolog_u_decay_1.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_1.text: So far a solution has eluded us. We're performing deep research in the background to figure this out.

audiolog_u_decay_1.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_1.text: And one day we may; meanwhile, we have to stay afloat: just slow the rot. Beat it back. Preserve.

audiolog_u_decay_2.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_2.text: My primary task: discover what we don't yet understand

audiolog_u_decay_2.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_2.text: about the laws of the Ultimate Ensemble, and the related holography.

audiolog_u_decay_2.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_2.text: The audacity of the goal is invigorating to many.

audiolog_u_decay_2.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_2.text: It's our new tetratetrad, but better, because it involves the potential for discovery of new fundamental laws.

audiolog_u_decay_2.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_2.text: My team has made some strides -- small strides, but they represent

audiolog_u_decay_2.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_2.text: the first addition to that area of Natural Philosophy in 200 years.

audiolog_u_decay_2.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_2.text: We may learn to cleanse the decay. We may learn to build space made of stronger stuff.

audiolog_u_decay_2.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_2.text: In the meantime, we need to isolate and fortify the areas proximal to the rot, *this* Warehouse being one of the worst.

audiolog_u_decay_3.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_3.text: We know that our problems have to do with the connectedness of the whole --

audiolog_u_decay_3.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_3.text: the whole of all space configured by our Order, together, space which is causally intertwined by its connective arcs.

audiolog_u_decay_3.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_3.text: Somehow, the cross-correlation has become too dense.

audiolog_u_decay_3.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_3.text: Expanding the volume of the space doesn't help us any more -- diminishing returns,

audiolog_u_decay_3.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_3.text: like there is a kind of super-information, or super-causation, we don't yet understand.

audiolog_u_decay_3.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_3.text: Classical holography has an information density limit, that you measure in Planck-area units,

audiolog_u_decay_3.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_3.text: but here we face a tighter constraint -- something much worse, that kicks in for causally heterogeneous spaces.

audiolog_u_decay_3.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_3.text: Some think the bounds involve consciousness in some way, which I agree is possible,

audiolog_u_decay_3.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_3.text: given the way our projections interact with awareness via the Hook channels.

audiolog_u_decay_3.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_3.text: We've only just realized that fresh observers help with preservation:

audiolog_u_decay_3.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_3.text: those who have never before experienced a particular Warehouse,

audiolog_u_decay_3.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_3.text: when it's all new to them, somehow their activities strengthen the projections for a while.

audiolog_u_decay_3.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_3.text: So you, unexpected Visitor, have helped us a bit already,

audiolog_u_decay_3.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_3.text: and there are a few more Warehouses I'd like you to visit...

audiolog_u_decay_4.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_4.text: We are reclusive these days. The Lifeboat Societies were already spare in their interactions --

audiolog_u_decay_4.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_4.text: this is baked into our cultures at their moments of founding.

audiolog_u_decay_4.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_4.text: The decay has made our Order ... even solitarier.

audiolog_u_decay_4.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_4.text: If we stay connected to some other party, they become part of our causal cluster for that interval;

audiolog_u_decay_4.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_4.text: the increased density of the enlarged cluster accelerates the decay.

audiolog_u_decay_4.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_4.text: It's so funny. In our physical Ensemble, look at the incredible

audiolog_u_decay_4.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_4.text: amount of stuff that exists without any trouble: all those galaxies you see when looking into the sky, and all the incredible space beyond.

audiolog_u_decay_4.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_4.text: However God built the ceiling of that cathedral is still a mystery; our Order's ceiling is lower, and lacks vaulting.

audiolog_u_decay_4.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_4.text: To slow the decay, we have severed connection not just with outsiders, but also internally --

audiolog_u_decay_4.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_4.text: for example, the creations of the Static and Dynamic Brigades are firewalled from each other.

audiolog_u_decay_4.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_4.text: Some went off to start a disjoint colony sending only rare and cryptic communications — a low-density restart.

audiolog_u_decay_4.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_4.text: I wish them well and hope someday to see what they have achieved.

audiolog_u_decay_4.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_4.text: Given this degree of isolation, you can understand why there was a kerfuffle

audiolog_u_decay_4.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_4.text: among the Preservation Crew when you just *showed up*.

audiolog_u_decay_4.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_4.text: But ... ... what they don't know won't hurt them.

audiolog_u_decay_5.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_5.text: Some say we should destroy our older Warehouses to make room for new creations.

audiolog_u_decay_5.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_5.text: I find the very idea distasteful! And, I don't think it would work.

audiolog_u_decay_5.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_5.text: Even should we denature everything here, down to ash ...

audiolog_u_decay_5.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_5.text: well, it is the case that innumerable specks of dust look interchangeable to us humans,

audiolog_u_decay_5.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_5.text: but God knows the history and personal character of each and every one.

audiolog_u_decay_5.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_5.text: The amount of information never goes down.

audiolog_u_decay_5.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_5.text: All that happens is, when you burn things, your personal ignorance goes up.

audiolog_u_decay_5.name: director
audiolog_u_decay_5.text: The apparent distance between you and God grows.

audiolog_u_chaos_1.name: sokoban
audiolog_u_chaos_1.text: ... but even so, I simply don't understand how you can believe in a beneficient God --

audiolog_u_chaos_1.name: sokoban
audiolog_u_chaos_1.text: Your Acting said this is a survival tactic, and I understand that idea to a decent degree. But it seems you *really* believe it.

audiolog_u_chaos_1.name: sokoban
audiolog_u_chaos_1.text: It's a plain fact that events in the world are too tragic to have been authored by a God who holds our well-being in mind;

audiolog_u_chaos_1.name: sokoban
audiolog_u_chaos_1.text: surely it is clear to you that what befalls us is shaped by chaos.

audiolog_u_chaos_1.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_1.text: You're an engineer; you try to understand the order in the world

audiolog_u_chaos_1.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_1.text: so you can exploit it to build complicated things; isn't that so?

audiolog_u_chaos_1.name: sokoban
audiolog_u_chaos_1.text: That is true ... we can follow causation

audiolog_u_chaos_1.name: sokoban
audiolog_u_chaos_1.text: within simple systems, and use those systems' regularity to predict outcomes.

audiolog_u_chaos_1.name: sokoban
audiolog_u_chaos_1.text: This works up to a point. Beyond that point, the engineer loses his purchase.

audiolog_u_chaos_1.name: sokoban
audiolog_u_chaos_1.text: Outcomes become deeply unpredictable. The destinies of individual humans are shaped largely by randomness.

audiolog_u_chaos_1.name: sokoban
audiolog_u_chaos_1.text: Immense and deadly storms, sweeping away entire towns of good and innocent people;

audiolog_u_chaos_1.name: sokoban
audiolog_u_chaos_1.text: diseases wherein certain cells of the body randomly become corrupted, and turn upon the whole...

audiolog_u_chaos_1.name: sokoban
audiolog_u_chaos_1.text: No loving God would torture his children in this way.

audiolog_u_chaos_1.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_1.text: You started by saying "chaos" -- perhaps meaning cause-and-effect

audiolog_u_chaos_1.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_1.text: that proceeds through too many steps, too quickly, for our human brains to follow --

audiolog_u_chaos_1.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_1.text: and then you call this "randomness", meaning things that are arbitrary and have no meaning.

audiolog_u_chaos_1.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_1.text: I would say these are improper words...

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: sokoban
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: I don't understand how you could know the maximum amount...

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: Yeah, you're making a face. You haven't yet achieved the arts of information processing in your world, then?

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: sokoban
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: Must not have; I can only vaguely guess at your meaning.

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: Push the button on your recorder there, so that you get down these words in my native language,

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: and your assignment will be to use the library -- we'll get someone to show you the library, it's really neat actually! --

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: to research anything you need, in depth, using these specific words to ensure accuracy, until you understand these statements:

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: Information can be represented by a certain number of bits.

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: For any fixed number of bits -- say you have a certain amount of physical space in which to write, one symbol per box --

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: there's a limit to the amount of information the symbols can hold.

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: If you just naively write facts into those bits, you will run out of space, falling woefully short of the potential that you *could* have reached.

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: But you can improve the amount of information you can fit, by finding shorter ways to write equivalent sentences.

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: If there's a long word, you could just stop writing as soon as it's unambiguous; instead of "armchair", you stop after "armch", and rely on your reader to complete the word.

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: If there are frequent long sequences of words, replace those with a few letters. If you find you write "it's a lovely morning" very often,

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: replace this with "kzq", and instruct the reader on this substitution.

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: So you start compressing the facts, finding shorter ways to write, so you can fit more facts into the space.

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: The methods of compression become quite sophisticated. The more you compress, the harder your message is to read --

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: because anyone wishing to understand it needs to perform the inverse operation to decompress.

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: And the more you compress, the more difficult it is to find ways to compress further.

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: Near the limit, improving the compression requires a tremendous amount of effort --

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: one might say a Godly amount of effort -- to make any further gains.

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: Until, finally, you have achieved perfection -- the message cannot possibly be made smaller, and the result you have encoded,

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: to the untrained eye, appears as completely random noise.

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: Now let's look at another scenario. One day, you find a slip of paper with some series of numbers written down;

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: you perform some statistical tests, and it seems completely random insofar as you can tell... well, you still don't know its actual nature.

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: Is it random, and thus you might call it completely meaningless?

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: Or is it a well-compressed message, with potentially a very deep meaning?

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: Both of these things appear maximally entropic, so you don't know. You *can't* know.

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: Same with an enciphered message. In the beginning, when developing the art of encipherment, you only know naive ways of obscuring what you wrote;

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: a clever spy can study the structure that remains in your encoded message, and work out the rules of encipherment, and thereby read the message.

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: But as you become better at encipherment, this conspicuous structure disappears,

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: and the message becomes nearly impossible to crack. Because it looks exactly like randomness.

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: A well-enciphered message, looks almost exactly like a well-compressed message, looks almost exactly like randomness.

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: So which is it? Which of these three models best represents the Universe in which we live?

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: Enciphered, compressed, or random?

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: I realize this doesn't mean much to you yet. But it's worth learning, even if only as a guiding image.

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: So. Any time that life looks scrambled, or chaotic, or meaningless...

audiolog_u_chaos_2.name: director
audiolog_u_chaos_2.text: It may just be that you lack the decipherment key.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0.text: This was our initial design for this puzzle. We decided it was too difficult,

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0.text: so we revised it to be easier (and you'll see that revision next).

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0.text: What's better or worse is always contextual.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0.text: In a short game, this version might be better than the revision, because it's more mysterious and difficult.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0.text: Many designers and players would tell you that some of their most memorable moments

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0.text: happened when a challenge looked completely impossible: you enter the level, you see it, it's simple, there's obviously no solution.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0.text: Then you notice one little thing, and it breaks the whole puzzle open.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0.text: If you haven't been spoiled already, spend some time solving this before listening to the second recording...

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.text: Over the course of development, we gained a lot of clarity about difficulty: when a puzzle is hard, it could be hard in a good way, or hard in a bad way.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.text: Suppose a puzzle is very difficult straight off. You enter the level, you look at it,

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.text: and it just doesn't give you any idea how to get started.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.text: That can be okay in isolation, but when this happens puzzle after puzzle after puzzle in a long game,

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.text: you're having the same experience over and over -- the experience of being stuck and confused.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.text: In a sense, they are all kind of the same puzzle, regardless of their specifics.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.text: This becomes tedious. You are working hard with very little reward;

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.text: it's just like banging your head against a brick wall. So you get tired and maybe you want to quit.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.text: That's not a great experience for you, but for *us*, that's not actually the worst part.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.text: The worst part is, because you spent almost all your time just trying random ideas, with no clear focus,

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.text: your thoughtspace is cluttered, and it's hard to see the core ideas that these levels were trying to communicate.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.text: If on a typical level you spend an hour just trying random stuff,

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.text: and only understand what you're meant to do in the last 5 minutes,

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.text: then only a small fraction of your experience is spent seeing and appreciating the neat ideas that are supposed to be the value delivered by the game.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.text: Early in development, we thought we were making puzzles better by maximizing

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.text: the amount of manipulation you had to do with objects in a level;

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.text: but over time we became more discerning about difficulty, and I sought to remove this kind of grindy excess Sokobanning.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.text: We want you to be spending time and energy on things that are unique to this game.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v0_part_2.text: You'll see how we improved the puzzle by changing it drastically in the revised version.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.text: Here, we've redesigned the level so it's immediately obvious that you need to make a stack.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.text: There's no other way to get the other guy to the exit.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.text: So, the only real question is how to make the stack; if you get stuck for a while figuring that out, that's okay,

audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.text: because you've been thinking about making a stack, and that's the idea that we want you to wrangle with here.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.text: Making it clear that you need to make a stack causes the puzzle to be easier, but in a long game,

audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.text: this helps you flow through the puzzles more quickly, one after another;

audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.text: this way you can see the flow of ideas better, because the ideas are more concentrated in time.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.text: This thing I just said is part of a non-obvious way of thinking about puzzles, so I'll make an analogy:

audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.text: Imagine listening to your favorite song -- the musical vibrations go into your ear, your brain appreciates the melody.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.text: If you slow that song down by a factor of two, maybe it's not so enjoyable any more; the tempo is off, the pitches of the notes are weird.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.text: But let's slow it down much more, by a factor of 20; at that point, it doesn't even work as music any more.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.text: It might be hard to hear anything at all, and to the extent you do, it's just weird low vibrations.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.text: Your brain can no longer hear the fun changes between notes in a musical way. You certainly wouldn't get into a groove.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.text: There's a particular range of time scales in which things are understandable and feel good.

audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_catching_up_v2.text: Now apply that to feeling the ideas shown to you by puzzles, as those ideas float invisibly in the space around you.

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7.text: This is Jonah's original design for one of the earliest Thief levels.

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7.text: The idea is that the Thief can only pull a Crystal onto the Button

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7.text: by going one specific way, and once she gets it there,

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7.text: she can't help but pull the Crystal back off the Button,

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7.text: shutting the Gate once again. Which is funny.

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7.text: You can also make the observation that the regular columns are a difficult structure for the Thief,

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7.text: because she can't ever get the crystal around one of those corners:

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7.text: she can only turn in the intersections,

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7.text: so she always has to leave the crystal at the side of a column.

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7.text: Here, at the beginning of the level, if she pulls the crystal any way but North, she's stuck.

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7.text: If I look through a pair of Design Elegance Goggles, the northwest area of the map looks pretty awkward; it isn't really used,

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7.text: except to suggest the continuation of the grid.

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.text: Here's the way I revised Jonah's idea into a completely different level.

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.text: It's much bigger, an atypical size for early Heroes, but I liked it so I kept it that way.

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.text: My goal was to give the player more practice using the Thief, and internalizing how she moves,

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.text: while also making a level that was easier to see the point of --

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.text: there was something about the original version that never left any meaningful takeaway in my brain.

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.text: Because this is an early training level, I wanted to use shapes that you see often throughout the game --

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.text: the columns in Jonah's version just aren't something you see much.

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.text: So, here we have a series of rooms connected by halls.

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.text: We maintain the funny situation with the button,

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.text: but we emphasize it by starting the Thief right next to the button (she's likely to walk onto it as her first move),

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.text: and placing the crystal far away. It's easy to walk to the crystal,

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.text: but not so simple to drag it back through the rooms.

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.text: The rooms are a little bit ridiculous in terms of the number of detours required

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.text: just to get the crystal where you want it.

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.text: This design is me having fun with the Thief's movement patterns;

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.text: but you could also say that the map of the level is *an illustration* of the Thief's movement patterns,

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.text: in that the room borders show a boundary that maximizes interest.

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.text: In this version of the level, we abandoned the original idea about columns and corners.

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.text: Instead, it's about walls: the Thief cannot ever pull an object up to a wall,

audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_heroes_1_7_v2.text: and this is part of what makes things silly.

audiolog_di_strategic_stack.name: director
audiolog_di_strategic_stack.text: This is Zach's original version. It's a neat idea for a level,

audiolog_di_strategic_stack.name: director
audiolog_di_strategic_stack.text: but the geometry doesn't help you see the idea at all.

audiolog_di_strategic_stack.name: director
audiolog_di_strategic_stack.text: The path to the goal island is indirect and very hard to visualize...

audiolog_di_strategic_stack.name: director
audiolog_di_strategic_stack.text: and you need to have some inkling of how to reach the goal

audiolog_di_strategic_stack.name: director
audiolog_di_strategic_stack.text: before you can start engaging with the core idea, which is about using a Mirror in a place

audiolog_di_strategic_stack.name: director
audiolog_di_strategic_stack.text: that helps you in the beginning, but later blocks you.

audiolog_di_strategic_stack.name: director
audiolog_di_strategic_stack.text: So, the lack of clarity in reading this level makes it difficult and frustrating to begin with. But then, on top of that, add this:

audiolog_di_strategic_stack.name: director
audiolog_di_strategic_stack.text: With 3 Mirrors and a Crystal, the natural impulse is to clone the Crystal a bunch of times, which doesn't actually help you here.

audiolog_di_strategic_stack.name: director
audiolog_di_strategic_stack.text: Indeed, it may seem that the level is *telling you* to clone the crystal, since you've seen other levels that tell you to clone crystals.

audiolog_di_strategic_stack.name: director
audiolog_di_strategic_stack.text: So not only is the correct pathway buried in obscurity, but the level is actively misleading you.

audiolog_di_strategic_stack.name: director
audiolog_di_strategic_stack.text: So if a player spends most of his time here just being lost and confused, it's no surprise.

audiolog_di_triple_gate.name: director
audiolog_di_triple_gate.text: Here's Patrick's revision. The core idea is similar (teleporting a crystal out from beneath a Mirror),

audiolog_di_triple_gate.name: director
audiolog_di_triple_gate.text: but the reason why you do it is totally different;

audiolog_di_triple_gate.name: director
audiolog_di_triple_gate.text: and, here, you do it twice, which feels better

audiolog_di_triple_gate.name: director
audiolog_di_triple_gate.text: and helps to cement the idea in your mind.

audiolog_di_triple_gate.name: director
audiolog_di_triple_gate.text: Most importantly, unlike the original version, it's very obvious what route you're trying to take,

audiolog_di_triple_gate.name: director
audiolog_di_triple_gate.text: so the Player spends no time being confused about that.

audiolog_di_triple_gate.name: director
audiolog_di_triple_gate.text: He just knows that he has to get past the Gates somehow.

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: This was conceived as a level about using a Mirror to reorient a dragon;

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: in order to roast Goblins in all 4 cardinal directions.

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: Because this was designed back when we felt we had to make levels generally difficult,

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: and require careful Sokoban moves, the area you're trapped inside is fairly tight:

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: to solve the puzzle, you need to do some careful repositioning.

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: Later, after we had built up our aesthetic about when difficulty is worthwhile and productive,

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: I felt this level was too cramped.

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: It's frustrating because you keep killing yourself

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: by stepping in the line of the Dragon's breath (usually when it's reflected off the Mirror, where you see no warning).

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: In such a small space, this becomes hard to avoid,

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: so a significant fraction of your moves are tweaky pre-positioning,

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: so you can then push the Mirror where you want it without dying.

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: In the revisions of this level, you'll see that we made the central chamber bigger;

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: that's one of the main reasons this level is presented here,

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: to show how the amount of space affects playability.

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: Besides being too cramped, there are at least two other serious flaws with this design.

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: Firstly, it's easy to mirror the Goblins into the chamber, or to a different side of the perimeter;

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: so if a player has an unclear idea of the puzzle, and is just experimenting, it's natural for him to make an un-fun mess.

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: It also means you don't actually need to shoot fire in all 4 directions,

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: because you can re-use some directions by teleporting the Goblins,

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: and this damages the core idea: We want all four directions!

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: The second problem is that the "surprise last step" of killing the 5th Goblin

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: is pretty hard to figure out, and that defocuses the level,

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: because you spend all this mental effort on something that does not involve shooting fire in four directions.

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: It's a good ending in the sense that you need to figure out something very specific,

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: but it's also somewhat arbitrary; yes, it is about orienting the dragon in a specific way,

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: but this just doesn't feel very connected to what you did previously.

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: Because this ending is hard,

audiolog_di_torcher.name: director
audiolog_di_torcher.text: it can become much larger in your memory than the thing we wanted you to remember.

audiolog_di_quad_torch_v1.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch_v1.text: Here, we've gone from a 5x5 central chamber to 7x7. This makes the main part of the puzzle easier, and perhaps here it's too easy.

audiolog_di_quad_torch_v1.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch_v1.text: To me it seemed overly straightforward; as the Player, I just felt

audiolog_di_quad_torch_v1.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch_v1.text: "Okay, I did the steps you told me to, therefore I won the level. So what?"

audiolog_di_quad_torch_v1.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch_v1.text: We want to avoid that feeling whenever we can, because this is a game, not a homework assignment.

audiolog_di_quad_torch_v1.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch_v1.text: Due to the solid outer wall, it's not as easy to mirror the Goblins, so you can no longer make a complete mess;

audiolog_di_quad_torch_v1.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch_v1.text: but you can clear one of the islands on the east or south

audiolog_di_quad_torch_v1.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch_v1.text: and then mirror the other Goblin onto that island,

audiolog_di_quad_torch_v1.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch_v1.text: so the basic problem still exists --

audiolog_di_quad_torch_v1.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch_v1.text: but the situation is improved, because you can't mirror Goblins to arbitrary messy places in the middle.

audiolog_di_quad_torch_v1.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch_v1.text: This version also has a "surprise last step" of drowning the dragon,

audiolog_di_quad_torch_v1.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch_v1.text: but it's easy to figure out, in contrast to the earlier revision;

audiolog_di_quad_torch_v1.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch_v1.text: so it feels more like a satisfying piece of ending punctuation than a difficult task that takes over the level.

audiolog_di_quad_torch.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch.text: Here we have another 7x7 chamber, but now it has a wall in the middle.

audiolog_di_quad_torch.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch.text: The wall takes up a little bit of slack space, but it also gives you another way

audiolog_di_quad_torch.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch.text: to cross the line of dragon breath when you want to.

audiolog_di_quad_torch.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch.text: This means the puzzle is less about crossing dragon breath,

audiolog_di_quad_torch.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch.text: and more about aiming and positioning the dragon.

audiolog_di_quad_torch.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch.text: You don't have to do a bunch of excess Sokobanning

audiolog_di_quad_torch.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch.text: to deal with the fact that you are crammed in.

audiolog_di_quad_torch.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch.text: The central column also helps solve the Goblin teleportation problem.

audiolog_di_quad_torch.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch.text: The Goblins on the east and south are set back,

audiolog_di_quad_torch.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch.text: so you can't teleport them into the chamber; if you wanted to teleport one Goblin to the other's spot,

audiolog_di_quad_torch.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch.text: as you could in the previous revision, you would have to place the Mirror where the central column is.

audiolog_di_quad_torch.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch.text: And of course you can't do that.

audiolog_di_quad_torch.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch.text: So, in this version, you do *finally* have to shoot fire in all 4 directions.

audiolog_di_quad_torch.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch.text: You could argue that the "kill the final monster" surprise here is a little off-topic,

audiolog_di_quad_torch.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch.text: but it does involve teleporting the dragon to the right place in the right orientation,

audiolog_di_quad_torch.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch.text: then escaping the cage, which is fun.

audiolog_di_quad_torch.name: director
audiolog_di_quad_torch.text: And it's tuned to be easier than the original version of the level.

audiolog_di_height_chooser.name: director
audiolog_di_height_chooser.text: The core idea of this level is to set up a situation with an Endpoint Beam and magic Mirror

audiolog_di_height_chooser.name: director
audiolog_di_height_chooser.text: such that you can choose how high you want to go up, teleport to that height,

audiolog_di_height_chooser.name: director
audiolog_di_height_chooser.text: and be held aloft by the Beam so that you can step onto the platform.

audiolog_di_height_chooser.name: director
audiolog_di_height_chooser.text: But there's a lot of other stuff going on. Having to fill the far endpoint of the purple Beam;

audiolog_di_height_chooser.name: director
audiolog_di_height_chooser.text: only being able to use the Lily once to go to the far shore;

audiolog_di_height_chooser.name: director
audiolog_di_height_chooser.text: the ability to recall the skipping stone with the magic Mirror,

audiolog_di_height_chooser.name: director
audiolog_di_height_chooser.text: and maybe change its direction of movement while it's skipping;

audiolog_di_height_chooser.name: director
