audiolog_di_height_chooser.text: questions about whether you are supposed to somehow use the Lily more than once,

audiolog_di_height_chooser.name: director
audiolog_di_height_chooser.text: whether you are supposed to sink the skipping stone to make terrain, and so forth.

audiolog_di_height_chooser.name: director
audiolog_di_height_chooser.text: It's just too much uncertainty about what's going on, in a place where the core scenario is already complicated and hard to see.

audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.name: director
audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.text: This is the version we ended up going with. It's the same basic idea, but we simplified it:

audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.name: director
audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.text: the concepts of Water, Skipping, and Lily have all been removed.

audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.name: director
audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.text: You have to set up the Crystal to block the Beam,

audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.name: director
audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.text: but the way you do this is more interesting, and it's actually on-topic for the level.

audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.name: director
audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.text: By putting the purple Beam on the far side of the level, instead of on top,

audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.name: director
audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.text: we make it easier to return to that side and move it, which reduces the amount of grindy Sokobanning.

audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.name: director
audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.text: This version is easier, but also better, because you are much more focused on the core idea.

audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.name: director
audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.text: This level is included in this collection to show the kind of improvement you can make when simplifying a level.

audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.name: director
audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.text: In the original version, certain design subtasks needed to be accomplished: you need to fill the purple endpoint in order to float.

audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.name: director
audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.text: But the way we implemented those subtasks created too much confusion for the player.

audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.name: director
audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.text: In general, whenever you design a puzzle and it's not as clean as you'd like,

audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.name: director
audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.text: you can look at individual subtasks and ask whether you *really* needed to do that thing in that specific way,

audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.name: director
audiolog_di_height_chooser_v0.text: or whether it can be done in a cleaner way.

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.text: The idea here is, you need to set up these stones so that, once you drop down,

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.text: you'll be able to push them onto the buttons ...

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.text: but due to tricky button positioning and the shape of the plateau,

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.text: it's difficult to see how to cover all the buttons at the same time.

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.text: This level is divided into two distinct parts,

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.text: a setup phase and a button-pushing phase;

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.text: this means it's mostly about pre-planning, because once you drop down, you can't change your crystal placement.

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.text: So, the level feels like a big mental maze where you are looking

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.text: at the shape of the plateau and what you can do with it.

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.text: I like this level a lot; it calls explicit attention to the process of solving a mental maze.

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.text: At the same time, though, you do mental mazes in a lot of puzzle games, so maybe this is not as special as we would like.

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.text: One thing to note about the maze design here:

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.text: it's mostly about whether you can push crystals away from the plateau or not.

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.text: In a few cases the answer is "Yes, I can get the crystal out if I push it in front of this hole, then drop down into the hole,"

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.text: but you can only use that trick once, so you have to detect

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot.text: the button that cannot be reached in any other way.

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.text: Here, we've simplified the level from 8 buttons to 6, while preserving most of the original ideas.

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.text: I say 'most' because one idea has been cut from this version,

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.text: which we mentioned in the previous recording: the part where you *could* reach several different buttons

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.text: by pushing a crystal in front of a hole, and then dropping into that hole,

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.text: but you can only do this once, so you choose the right hole to drop into.

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.text: In this revision, we've streamlined the concepts: "Here are a variety of ways you could reach the buttons,

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.text: and just one of them involves dropping into a hole".

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.text: The original version of this level is a bigger, more difficult mental maze.

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.text: Because this one is not so big, you spend less time maze-solving, and proportionately more time

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.text: just looking at the individual cases of where the crystals can go.

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.text: To me, it's a little bit of a matter of taste which version you like more.

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.text: You might think this one is too easy; but as a designer, keep in mind

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.text: that it's easy to underestimate the difficulty, because you know the answer already, because you came up with it!

audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.name: director
audiolog_di_push_down_a_lot_small.text: In the interest of keeping the pacing quick and avoiding redundant material, we went with the simpler version.

audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.name: director
audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.text: My experience was that it's pretty hard, and I often didn't have a clear idea of what I was trying to accomplish,

audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.name: director
audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.text: until I managed to stumble to the goal; then, even at the end,

audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.name: director
audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.text: I couldn't quite tell you the idea of the puzzle,

audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.name: director
audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.text: except that it's about going back and forth between the rooms, which as I mentioned, is hard.

audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.name: director
audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.text: I'm not saying this to denigrate the puzzle -- I think it's good and interesting,

audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.name: director
audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.text: but at the same time, sometimes you'll find yourself faced with this kind of situation,

audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.name: director
audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.text: where something just doesn't gel in the Player's mind the way you wish it did.

audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.name: director
audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.text: We don't know why Zach made this a Thief level;

audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.name: director
audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.text: the activity of Pulling does not have anything obvious to do with the core idea,

audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.name: director
audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.text: and it pushes the level toward being bigger, because the Thief cannot drag things to the wall.

audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.name: director
audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.text: This pollutes the level a bit, because the Thief's pulling ability is off topic.

audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.name: director
audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.text: I've spoken elsewhere about how we try to avoid adding irrelevant objects and ideas to a level.

audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.name: director
audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.text: So in a level like this one, where you just need to move things and it doesn't matter how,

audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.name: director
audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.text: it's cleaner and simpler to use a character who can only push one thing,

audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.name: director
audiolog_di_across_the_fence_old.text: because pushing one thing in this game is "the default idea" and introduces the least noise.

audiolog_di_across_the_fence_vtrader_m_p.name: director
audiolog_di_across_the_fence_vtrader_m_p.text: Here we've shrunk the level substantially, and the Trader is now the main character,

audiolog_di_across_the_fence_vtrader_m_p.name: director
audiolog_di_across_the_fence_vtrader_m_p.text: which removes the distracting question of whether Pulling matters;

audiolog_di_across_the_fence_vtrader_m_p.name: director
audiolog_di_across_the_fence_vtrader_m_p.text: now the level uses ingredients from only two worlds,

audiolog_di_across_the_fence_vtrader_m_p.name: director
audiolog_di_across_the_fence_vtrader_m_p.text: instead of the three we had before, and that's simpler too.

audiolog_di_sender.name: director
audiolog_di_sender.text: This one is about disappearing a Monster by teleporting it to infinity, in the vertical direction.

audiolog_di_sender.name: director
audiolog_di_sender.text: Which is a neat idea, but requires some contrivance to set up.

audiolog_di_sender.name: director
audiolog_di_sender.text: This first attempt is a little hard to read initially,

audiolog_di_sender.name: director
audiolog_di_sender.text: and is somewhat misleading because it places the Goblin

audiolog_di_sender.name: director
audiolog_di_sender.text: into a suspicious position, where you can teleport it directly onto the button --

audiolog_di_sender.name: director
audiolog_di_sender.text: which is not part of the solution.

audiolog_di_sender_simplified.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified.text: Here's another attempt at this level. Now there's only one character, who can go up and down at will.

audiolog_di_sender_simplified.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified.text: I didn't want to add an Elevator, so I used a second Gate for you to go up and down,

audiolog_di_sender_simplified.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified.text: which I felt was more on-theme... you raise an object with a Gate to get it to the plateau,

audiolog_di_sender_simplified.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified.text: and later you raise a Goblin with the other Gate to make it disappear.

audiolog_di_sender_simplified.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified.text: Ideally I'd have wanted to figure out how to do both of these raisings with one Gate, but I never did. So there are two Gates,

audiolog_di_sender_simplified.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified.text: with weird geometry around them, and it's now very hard to read the level --

audiolog_di_sender_simplified.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified.text: you need to do a bunch of Sokobanning to set up the final trick of the level, but this is very hard to visualize in advance.

audiolog_di_sender_simplified.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified.text: You might think this is some kind of ideal of tight puzzle design, using objects for several different purposes;

audiolog_di_sender_simplified.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified.text: for example you use the Gem to push the Goblin around and also to power the socket,

audiolog_di_sender_simplified.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified.text: but in this case it just fogs up the core idea.

audiolog_di_sender_simplified.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified.text: Compare this to the previous version, which had a vertical Gate

audiolog_di_sender_simplified.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified.text: with no apparent function out in the middle of the floor --

audiolog_di_sender_simplified.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified.text: You come into the level, and, obviously you are supposed to do something with that Gate, but what?

audiolog_di_sender_simplified.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified.text: It gave you something very clear to notice and think about. And that's missing from this version.

audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.text: This version of the level, which we chose as the final,

audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.text: is even more economical than the previous one:

audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.text: we've gotten rid of the weird confusing geometry and the double vertical Gates.

audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.text: Because raising objects to the upper level is not part of the core idea, we have streamlined that out:

audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.text: the gem and Beamcaster start at the top, and you just need to move them down.

audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.text: It's still a little difficult, and the vertical Gate is slightly obfuscated because you use it to get up to the plateau;

audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.text: but because there's only one Gate, and nothing else to do, it's still a focus.

audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.text: The way it's slightly hidden feels fairer, and more like a stylistic flourish.

audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.text: This version of the level is still perhaps a little harder than it "should" be,

audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.text: since even after you get the basic idea of what to do, it's easy to get a little confused.

audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.text: At least for me, the temptation is to try to use both the Beamcaster and the Gem

audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.text: to push the Goblin horizontally in X and Y so it's next to the Gate,

audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.text: and then somehow get the Beamcaster down to the bottom without being killed.

audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.text: This can't be done; instead, you want to put the Beamcaster on the lower level first.

audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.text: We could eliminate this extra confusion by starting the Beamcaster on the bottom (since it'd be impossible to get it onto the plateau),

audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.text: but then maybe we are closer to just giving the player the answer, which doesn't feel good to me.

audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.text: All of this is subjective, and you could come to your own conclusion.

audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.text: But I think, because this is a late-game level, maybe some extra difficulty is okay.

audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.text: Look how ugly the previous two versions were, geometrically, compared to this one.

audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.text: Most puzzles can be improved through this kind of iteration.

audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.text: It's a little humbling to know that your puzzles could always be better,

audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.text: and for a game of significant size, it's very very hard

audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_sender_simplified_v2.text: to get anywhere close to the best versions of all the puzzles.

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: This level went through a number of revisions, being simplified each time.

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: Here's the initial version, where on the left side,

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: we have an excuse for the Strength beam to be there -- he needs it to get the Displacer --

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: whereas the Strength beam is really there so that the Priestess can push things.

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: Ideally, the Priestess pushing the Monsters would be interesting and fun, but here it's kind of a slog

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: because there are multiple solutions, and they are all a little hard to see;

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: this makes the blocking crystals feel less intentional, and more random.

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: Also, the Player will probably wonder if he is supposed to use the Double beam for something besides exiting the level (but he isn't).

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: In this version, we've gotten rid of all the crystals, which helps the level feel focused.

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: We also got rid of the Double beam, and allowed ourselves the slight impurity of placing a Monster Gate on the Beamcaster side.

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: We've also made the Monster elimination less messy and more focused:

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: there are 5 Goblins, so you obviously need to make a group of 3,

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: but this can't be done without moving one away from the wall using the Displacer,

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: which is a second way the two sides can affect each other.

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: We continued to revise.

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: Here, we got rid of the Rocks on the Beamcaster side,

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: since they served no interesting purpose, except that you would displace one of them through the wall between the worlds --

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: for that purpose, we have placed a second Gem instead.

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: The fact that there are two Gems and only one socket

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: should immediately raise questions about what the second Gem is for.

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: Instead of 5 monsters, we cut it down to 3,

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: so the challenge is clearly to put all 3 together.

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: The Displacing is even more interesting now, since you have to use the Priestess herself

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: as additional mass to move the Goblin through the wall.

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: Unfortunately, though, there's a problem with this little Goblin room.

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: The intended solution is to displace him through the wall,

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: (after having moved the other Goblins north out of the way),

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: then south, east 1 square, and north, to make a 3-wide Goblin group.

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: But there's another solution, where you just push the two outer Goblins south by a square,

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: then zap the third guy through the wall to make a 3-wide group.

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: This isn't the worst exploit, since it's still the same basic idea,

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: but we wanted this level to require more use of the Strength Beam. So we fixed that in the next version...

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: Here we moved the location of the Power Socket, so that the Priestess can't push the two Goblins south,

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: fixing the exploit from the previous version.

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: We also made the third Goblin's area less of an enclosed room,

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: to avoid suggesting moves that are irrelevant, like displacing objects through

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: the longer stretch of wall that existed in that version of the level.

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: Perhaps this version of the level feels a couple rows too tall on the Heroes side,

audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.name: director
audiolog_di_worlds_collide_heroes_and_pr.text: but the Beamcaster side needs that space: you need two empty rows on the south to displace the Beamcaster back north.

audiolog_di_lily_wearing_intro.name: director
audiolog_di_lily_wearing_intro.text: This level showcases an unexpected and silly interaction

audiolog_di_lily_wearing_intro.name: director
audiolog_di_lily_wearing_intro.text: of Goblins wearing Lilies as hats -- The Goblins die in water, allowing the Lily to float.

audiolog_di_lily_wearing_intro.name: director
audiolog_di_lily_wearing_intro.text: The second island has a twist -- a second Goblin is in your way.

audiolog_di_lily_wearing_intro.name: director
audiolog_di_lily_wearing_intro.text: This is all nice, but the challenge that comes from pushing stones around in close quarters

audiolog_di_lily_wearing_intro.name: director
audiolog_di_lily_wearing_intro.text: is a bit extraneous to the overall topic of the level.

audiolog_di_tiger_lily_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_tiger_lily_v2.text: Here's Patrick's revision. The interaction is explored more thoroughly

audiolog_di_tiger_lily_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_tiger_lily_v2.text: and adds depth to the puzzle by requiring the player to figure out

audiolog_di_tiger_lily_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_tiger_lily_v2.text: exactly where to drop the Lilies in order to reach the next island.

audiolog_di_tiger_lily_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_tiger_lily_v2.text: Goblins were swapped out for Dragons. Dragons can be pushed without a stone in between,

audiolog_di_tiger_lily_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_tiger_lily_v2.text: which makes it quicker and more comfortable to experiment and execute ideas,

audiolog_di_tiger_lily_v2.name: director
audiolog_di_tiger_lily_v2.text: and allows for more complex puzzles while adding fewer objects to the level.

audiolog_u_meeting.name: acting
audiolog_u_meeting.text: Well! It's been a few years!

audiolog_u_meeting.name: acting
audiolog_u_meeting.text: So. You have that Certain Look. Are you here to relieve me?

audiolog_u_meeting.name: director
audiolog_u_meeting.text: I'm still out there ... investigating. You'll have to keep running things for now.

audiolog_u_meeting.name: director
audiolog_u_meeting.text: Or appoint a successor if you're tired.

audiolog_u_meeting.name: director
audiolog_u_meeting.text: It's going *somewhere*. Well or poorly, too soon to say.

audiolog_u_meeting.name: director
audiolog_u_meeting.text: This guy you want to promote to Sokoban.

audiolog_u_meeting.name: director
audiolog_u_meeting.text: Oh, I trust you. You've done it before, and that last one seems to have acclimated pretty well, strange as he is.

audiolog_u_meeting.name: director
audiolog_u_meeting.text: He's paying his dues. But regarding your *new* outlander Sokoban,

audiolog_u_meeting.name: director
audiolog_u_meeting.text: I want to have some conversations with him. For reasons relating to my inquiry.

audiolog_u_meeting.name: acting
audiolog_u_meeting.text: I should arrange for you to speak alone?

audiolog_u_meeting.name: director
audiolog_u_meeting.text: The topics will wander. You can nose in, if you want.

audiolog_u_computation.name: sokoban
audiolog_u_computation.text: Ahh, the Clayson's Field. Though we only know it by still images in books and papers;

audiolog_u_computation.name: sokoban
audiolog_u_computation.text: I've never seen this kind of smooth rendition. Beautiful!

audiolog_u_computation.name: director
audiolog_u_computation.text: It's one of the simplest examples of running rules on repeated state --

audiolog_u_computation.name: director
audiolog_u_computation.text: where the starting state itself is just always zero.

audiolog_u_computation.name: director
audiolog_u_computation.text: Square it, add the two-dimensional constant for that position in the plane, and that's the new number, and repeat.

audiolog_u_computation.name: director
audiolog_u_computation.text: See how long your number survives, and color accordingly. And, you see ...

audiolog_u_computation.name: director
audiolog_u_computation.text: Glad you understand. I'll give you this to play with. The important thing to internalize --

audiolog_u_computation.name: director
audiolog_u_computation.text: and absorb over and over in an attempt to understand ever-more-deeply --

audiolog_u_computation.name: director
audiolog_u_computation.text: is that the math is so simple, obviously we don't put the complexity in there, ourselves.

audiolog_u_computation.name: director
audiolog_u_computation.text: + instant_duration 5.6 That complexity and structure is just *already there* somehow. It's fundamental.

audiolog_u_computation.name: director
audiolog_u_computation.text: How about this one, have you seen it?

audiolog_u_computation.name: sokoban
audiolog_u_computation.text: No, ... no idea what that is.

audiolog_u_computation.name: director
audiolog_u_computation.text: I'll leave you to play with it. This one is called "Life",

audiolog_u_computation.name: director
audiolog_u_computation.text: named long ago, conceived as an analogy for biological cells reproducing and dying.

audiolog_u_computation.name: director
audiolog_u_computation.text: It's another example of applying simple rules, repeatedly, to initial world state.

audiolog_u_computation.name: director
audiolog_u_computation.text: This time the rules are exactly the same at every point in the space.

audiolog_u_computation.name: director
audiolog_u_computation.text: Experiment; see what you can figure out.

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.text: ... and that's how we travel to spaces that are far,

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.text: or completely disconnected -- like the worlds you see in this Warehouse.

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.text: Because the universe acts holographically -- as we first gleaned from the study of black holes --

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.name: sokoban
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.text: Yes, your Acting Director told me about those...

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.text: I suspect you have them too, just haven't found them yet.

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.text: Anyway, the upshot is, everything inside a volume of space is determined by some information at the boundary.

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.text: The exact nature of that information is hard to explain, as it's all mixed up together.

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.text: But, if there's someplace you want to go, and you're able to duplicate the conditions on its boundary,

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.text: by changing the boundary of the place you're starting from, to match precisely --

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.text: then you can swap the two boundaries and all contents therein.

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.text: The *amount* of energy is proportional to the surface area,

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.text: but it's not really so much for smaller spaces. Not compared to what we have available, anyway.

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.text: Funny how this line of inquiry started; they were trying to resolve all these historical cases where it had been raining fish --

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.text: just fish falling from the sky, a natural phenomenon confirmed repeatedly,

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.text: including by reliable observers. No plausible explanation.

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.text: So a guy is thinking hard about how this could happen. He comes up with this boundary-swapping idea,

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.text: and, after years, gets it to work on tiny tiny things. He builds it up to handle macroscopic and eventually human-sized spaces.

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.text: And now we can travel.

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.text: But in the end he realized that boundary swapping couldn't explain the fish.

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.text: The boundary conditions would just have been too different; unmatchable.

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.text: So that's a mystery we never solved, and won't any time soon,

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_1.text: since the Earth as we knew it is now long gone...

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.name: sokoban
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.text: Am I to take it that this boundary business is how you *find* the worlds, as well?

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.text: The full story is complicated, but that's part of it.

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.name: sokoban
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.text: These worlds are completely separated from yours; until you have been to your desired destination

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.name: sokoban
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.text: at least once, you have no measurement of it. How do you know what boundary to match?

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.text: If you are content with a volume that's extremely small,

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.text: you can take a guess what a boundary might look like inside the destination you want,

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.text: and keep trying til you get something.

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.text: Maybe you fail quite a number of times, but suppose, eventually, you successfully get a swap.

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.text: Your boundary is so small, it can fit just a few particles,

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.text: but they act as an initial sensor. That sensor gives you some information.

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.text: With that information, you try a slightly bigger boundary.

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.text: If you don't quite get it right, try perturbing things a little, at random.

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.text: When you succeed with the slightly bigger boundary, send a slightly bigger sensor. You get slightly more information.

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.text: + instant_duration 3.6 Keep repeating this until you fit inside the swapped space yourself.

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.text: It's complicated to describe the boundary conditions that actually matter.

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.text: Famously, you can't clone a quantum state, but here you don't need to, because a bunch of stuff cancels out.

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.name: sokoban
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.text: I'll keep that in mind, but first I shall need to learn about "quantum states".

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.text: Sure. Anyway, what's important is not the boundary conditions at any one point, or even all the points.

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.text: Because, again, it's all mixed up. Holography. What matters is the aggregate value,

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.text: and this lets us get away with some things that would be impossible otherwise.

audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.name: director
audiolog_u_boundary_matching_2.text: One might even think it was designed this way.

paradise_lost_invocation_credits.name: jon
paradise_lost_invocation_credits.text: Instruct me, for Thou know'st; Thou from the first Wast present, and with mighty wings outspread

paradise_lost_invocation_credits.name: jon
paradise_lost_invocation_credits.text: + instant_duration 5.5 Dove-like satst brooding on the vast Abyss And mad'st it pregnant:

paradise_lost_invocation_credits.name: jon
paradise_lost_invocation_credits.text: What in me is dark Illumin, what is low raise and support;

paradise_lost_invocation_credits.name: jon
paradise_lost_invocation_credits.text: + instant_duration 12 That to the highth of this great Argument I may assert Eternal Providence, And justifie the wayes of God to men.

paradise_lost_invocation_credits.name: jon
paradise_lost_invocation_credits.text: Unto ages of ages. Thy will be done. Amen.

end3_heroes_first.name: thief
end3_heroes_first.text: Sorry, friends... I get mixed up sometimes!

end3_thief_taunted.name: thief
end3_thief_taunted.text: Life's so strange... Sometimes I just feel like I'm being taunted!

end3_mirror_isles_first.name: trader
end3_mirror_isles_first.text: Nearly done here. Almost time to return home.

end3_mirror_isles_second.name: trader
end3_mirror_isles_second.text: I wonder how she'll react when she finds out I'm not dead.

end3_suit.name: gemsman
end3_suit.text: I spent so long fixing up this suit... then, so long *in* the suit...

end3_suit.name: gemsman
end3_suit.text: It'll be nice to be done for a bit.

coda.name: queen
coda.text: I am your ardent disciple, heir to your charge...

coda.name: queen
coda.text: If it be granted me to survive this day, I will guard these your relics

coda.name: queen
coda.text: for which we have searched *so long*... let them not be lost,

coda.name: queen
coda.text: let them be set forth for all to see, a beacon;

coda.name: queen
coda.text: and with your image in our people's hearts, stoking hope and inspiration, I will lead them forth into renewal.

coda.name: queen
coda.text: But if I am never to leave this place, if the road leads only into the Maw, let me go alone;

coda.name: queen
coda.text: let my men be not buried with me. Protect them, whom you must reward for their faithfulness,

coda.name: queen
coda.text: and bring them safely through this day, that they may return to their chidren and their wives.

coda.name: queen
coda.text: They will remember me alongside you, and our legend may yet shine into the future and do much good.

coda.name: jackays
coda.text: What dark enchantment... Queen, my Queen, where are you? Have they...

coda.name: jackays
coda.text: Not 10 seconds! You were ... just gone!

coda.name: queen
coda.text: Well then, you may finish your report.

coda.name: jackays
coda.text: It is an honor to fight for you, my Queen; stick close, we've no more time.

coda.name: jackays
coda.text: Inner Guard, rally! Hold nothing back, as we are surrounded!

coda.name: magistrate
coda.text: I believe I've found my new hobby. Now, who's next?...

pre_coda_scene_assembled.text: let my men be not buried with me. Protect them, whom you must reward for their faithfulness,

pre_coda_scene_assembled.name: director
pre_coda_scene_assembled.text: and bring them safely through this day, that they may return to their chidren and their wives.

pre_coda_scene_assembled.name: director
pre_coda_scene_assembled.text: They will remember me alongside you, and our legend may yet shine into the future and do much good.

pre_coda_scene_assembled.name: director
pre_coda_scene_assembled.text: What dark enchantment... Queen, my Queen, where are you?

paradise_lost_invocation_2.name: acting
paradise_lost_invocation_2.text: Dove-like satst brooding on the vast Abyss And mad'st it pregnant:

paradise_lost_invocation_2.name: acting
paradise_lost_invocation_2.text: What in me is dark Illumin, what is low raise and support;

paradise_lost_invocation_2.name: acting
paradise_lost_invocation_2.text: That to the highth of this great Argument I may assert Eternal Providence, And justifie the wayes of God to men.

psalm_139.name: acting
psalm_139.text: If I ascend up into heaven, thou art there:

psalm_139.name: acting
psalm_139.text: if I make my bed in hell, behold, thou art there.

psalm_139.name: acting
psalm_139.text: If I take the wings of the morning, and dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea;

psalm_139.name: acting
psalm_139.text: Even there shall thy hand lead me, and thy right hand shall hold me.

psalm_139.name: acting
psalm_139.text: If I say, Surely the darkness shall cover me; even the night shall be light about me.

psalm_139.name: acting
psalm_139.text: Yea, the darkness hideth not from thee; but the night shineth as the day:

psalm_139.name: acting
psalm_139.text: the darkness and the light are both alike to thee.

psalm_139_part_2.name: acting
psalm_139_part_2.text: I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made:

psalm_139_part_2.name: acting
psalm_139_part_2.text: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well.

psalm_139_part_2.name: acting
psalm_139_part_2.text: My substance was not hid from thee, when I was made in secret,

psalm_139_part_2.name: acting
psalm_139_part_2.text: and curiously wrought in the lowest parts of the earth.

psalm_139_part_2.name: acting
psalm_139_part_2.text: Thine eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect;

psalm_139_part_2.name: acting
psalm_139_part_2.text: and in thy book all my members were written,

psalm_139_part_2.name: acting
psalm_139_part_2.text: which in continuance were fashioned, when as yet there was none of them.

psalm_139_part_2.name: acting
psalm_139_part_2.text: How precious also are thy thoughts unto me, O God! how great is the sum of them!

psalm_139_part_2.name: acting
psalm_139_part_2.text: If I should count them, they are more in number than the sand:

psalm_139_part_2.name: acting
psalm_139_part_2.text: when I awake, I am still with thee.

audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.name: director
audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.text: Canst thou draw out leviathan with an hook? or his tongue with a cord which thou lettest down?

audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.name: director
audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.text: Will he make many supplications unto thee? Will he speak soft words unto thee?

audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.name: director
audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.text: Lay thine hand upon him, remember the battle, do no more.

audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.name: director
audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.text: I will not conceal his parts, nor his power, nor his comely proportion.

audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.name: director
audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.text: His scales are his pride, shut up together as with a close seal.

audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.name: director
audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.text: One is so near to another, that no air can come between them.

audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.name: director
audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.text: By his neesings a light doth shine, and his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.

audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.name: director
audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.text: His breath kindleth coals, and a flame goeth out of his mouth.

audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.name: director
audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.text: His heart is as firm as a stone; yea, as hard as a piece of the nether millstone.

audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.name: director
audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.text: When he raiseth up himself, the mighty are afraid: by reason of breakings they purify themselves.

audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.name: director
audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.text: He esteemeth iron as straw, and brass as rotten wood.

audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.name: director
audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.text: He laugheth at the shaking of a spear.

audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.name: director
audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.text: Upon earth there is not his like, who is made without fear.

audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.name: director
audiolog_u_job_41_fragments.text: He beholdeth all high things: he is a king over all the children of pride.
